title.narrative: Support to Strategic Note of UN Women Albania 2022-2026
Support to the Strategic Note UN Women 2022-2026 Albania

description.narrative:
The overall objective of the Strategic Note of UN Women in Albania 2022-20206 is:
All women and girls fully enjoy and exercise their human rights in a gender equal society and meaningfully contribute to Albania's sustainable and inclusive socio-economic development and EU integration.

NDetta är ett icke öronmärkt stöd till den strategiska rapporten från UN Women i Albanien 2022–2026. De tre huvudinriktningarna i den strategiska planen är: 1) Rättvisa investeringar i människor; 2) Produktiv utveckling för alla. 3) Jämställdhetsmedveten styrning. UN Women arbetar med partners för att bekämpa könsstereotyper, bland annat genom medier, medvetandehöjande åtgärder och kapacitetsuppbyggnad. På lokal nivå stöder UN Women det civila samhället, tjänsteleverantörer, lokalsamhällen och personal vid lokala myndigheter. På central nivå arbetar UN Women med flera fackministerier, statistiska institut (INSTAT), parlamentsledamöter, statens högsta revisionsorgan, nationella institutioner för mänskliga rättigheter, civilsamhällesorganisationer, den akademiska världen, den privata sektorn, media och andra. Inom ramen för dessa engagemang erbjuder UN Women kunskap, tekniskt stöd, policyrådgivning och exponering för bästa praxis globalt och från regionen om alla aspekter av jämställdhetsagendan.

This is un-earmarked support to the Strategic Note of UN Women in Albania 2022-2026. The three main directions of the Strategic Plan are: 1) Equitable investment in People; 2) Productive and Inclusive Development; 3) Gender Responsive Governance. UN Women works with partners to tackle gender stereotypes, including through media, awareness raising and building capacities. At local level, UN Women supports civil society, service providers, communities and staff of local governments. At the central level, UN Women works with several line ministries, statistical institute (INSTAT), members of Parliament, State Supreme Audit, National Human Rights Institutions, civil society organizations, academia, the private sector, media and others. Across these engagements, UN Women offers knowledge, technical support, policy advice and exposure to best practices globally and from the region on all aspects of the gender equality agenda.

title.narrative: Agreement UN Women Albania Strategic Note
Agreement UN Women Albania Strategic Note

description.narrative:
Outcome 1: More Equitable Investment in People:
In 2024, government institutions in Albania strengthened the design and delivery of services that meet the needs of women and vulnerable groups. A new National Strategy on Social Protection was adopted, featuring enhanced gender indicators, costed measures, and newly introduced concepts and actions related to intersectionality and the care economy. These additions signal a stronger institutional commitment to advancing the rights of women and girls. At local level, over 700 individuals more than half of whom are women actively participated in budget discussions across five municipalities. Their contributions directly shaped 32 community-led initiatives, the majority of which were addressed by local authorities.
Outcome 2: More Inclusive and Sustainable Development:
Women in Albania gained better access to resources and opportunities to grow their businesses and improve their livelihoods. In 2024, 40 women entrepreneurs joined the national women entrepreneurship EXPO, benefiting from training on digital tools and marketing, enhancing their ability to showcase their products and services, and connecting with over 100 attendees. As a result, several participants secured new business partnerships and increased sales, expanding their reach beyond local markets.
In rural areas, 35 women were able to strengthen their roles in the local economy thanks to increased business skills. For example, some women began selling to larger companies and improved their food safety practices.
Outcome 3: Stronger Gender-Responsive Governance:
Following up to a specific recommendation from the CEDAW Committee, the government began updating the Gender Equality Law to meet international standards. UN Women supported this process by providing expert advice and organizing public consultations. The government also increased its investments on gender equality. In 2024, 9.6% of the national budget was allocated for services that benefit women, such as support for survivors of violence and maternal health care. In the context of the Beijing 30 Global Action Agenda, the Government also announced a commitment to increase public investments for gender equality and women empowerment of an additional 1% annually until 2030.
More than 2,600 women accessed services for survivors of violence, and 683 women received legal assistance. Albania also launched its first Femicide Watch, which provides in depth analysis of gender-based killings, contributing to strengthen the overall risk assessment capacity of relevant institutions and help prevent gender-based violence. Public awareness campaigns challenging harmful gender stereotypes reached over 1.6 million people.
The UN system in Albania also improved its coordination on gender equality. Eleven out of fifteen performance indicators of the UNCT SWAP Gender Equality Scorecard showed strong results, while 45 UN staff were trained on how to include gender perspectives in their work.
